summary: El Dorado County tower in the Eldorado National Forest, now listed as gone; only 1913 and 1915 Mountain Democrat notes of fire guards were found.

facts.status_note: Index marks it gone; no source found describes the site today

staffing.status: first fire guard on duty in 1913; lookout fireman named for the 1915 season

events.note: Mountain Democrat, May 17, 1913: first fire guard in the El Dorado National Forest went on duty on the mountain; earliest record found
Mountain Democrat, June 19, 1915: O. R. Murdock of Georgetown named lookout fireman for the season and reported for duty

evidence.supports: county and forest: Eldorado County, Eldorado National Forest
attribution of both items to the Mountain Democrat
1913 date of the Mountain Democrat item
first fire guard went on duty on Lookout Mountain in 1913
evidence.quote: The first fire guard to be placed in the El Dorado National Forest went on duty last Thursday on Lookout Mountain, and men have been out repairing telephone lines in preparation for use during the fire season.

evidence.supports: 1915 date of the Mountain Democrat item
1915 lookout fireman named and reported for duty
evidence.quote: Mr. O.R. Murdock of Georgetown, who will act as lookout fireman during the ensuing fire season, reported for duty at Lookout Mt. on the 16th.

evidence.supports: index row: El Dorado County, tower, listed as gone
evidence.quote: Lookout Mountain El Dorado 38.88348 -120.56112 Tower Gone

notes_for_editor: Two Mountain Democrat excerpts (as transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page) and the index are the only sources. Two web searches found no Eldorado-specific hit. The forest's 2022 Fire Lookouts handout (fs.usda.gov/media/121933) was read and does not name this mountain. Next step if wanted: the Mountain Democrat archive (CDNC) for 1913 to 1930s, or Eldorado NF records. Index coordinates 38.88348, -120.56112.
